source_text: μάτων ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ· καὶ ψυχῆς μὲν εἰς τύπον τὸ αἷμα. Τέθεικε δὲ τὴν ψυχὴν ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, οὐχ ὑπέρ γε μόνης τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησίας, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐν νόμῳ, τουτέστι, τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ἐκλελυτρώμεθα γὰρ τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ συλλήβδην ἅπαντες, Ἕλληνές τε καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ μαρτυρήσει λέγων ὁ Παῦλος· «Ἢ Ἰουδαίων ὁ Θεὸς μόνον; οὐχὶ δὲ καὶ ἐθνῶν; ναὶ καὶ ἐθνῶν· εἴπερ εἷς ὁ Θεὸς, ὃς δικαιώσει περιτομὴν ἐκ πίστεως, καὶ ἀκροβυστίαν διὰ πίστεως.» Ὑφαιρομένων δὲ ἀπ' αὐτῶν τῶν ἐντοσθίων τοῦ μόσχου καὶ ἀναφερομένων εἰς τὸ θυσιαστήριον, ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς τὸ ἐπίλοιπον καταπίμπραται σῶμα. Ἔστι γὰρ αὐτὸς τὸ θῦμα τὸ ἱερὸν, εὐωδιάζων ἐν ἀρεταῖς, ὧν εἶεν ἂν τύποι τὰ ἐντόσθια, καὶ κεκρυμμέναι οἱονεί πως ἐν ἡμῖν αἱ ἀρεταὶ, καὶ εἰς νοῦν ἔσω κείμεναι· αὐτὸς καὶ ὁ πάσχων ἔξω τῆς πύλης, καὶ τῷ θανάτῳ τῆς ἰδίας σαρκὸς ἐκκαθαίρων τοὺς μεμολυσμένους· «Δαμάλεως γὰρ σποδὸς ῥαντίζουσα τοὺς κεκοινωμένους, ἁγιάζει, φησὶ, πρὸς τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καθαρότητα.» Οὐκοῦν εἷς καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς ὑπάρχων ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἁγίαις εὐωδιάζει σκηναῖς, φημὶ δὴ ταῖς Ἐκκλησίαις· πέπονθε δὲ καὶ ἔξω τῆς πύλης· ἔνθα καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξιέναι δεῖν τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν αὐτοῦ φέροντας, ὁ θεσπέσιος ἔφη Παῦλος. Προσάγεται δὲ ὁ μόσχος καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων, ἐν ἴσῳ τε καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτως· καὶ λόγος ἦν τῆς θυσίας ἐν ἅπασιν ὁ αὐτός. Ἐν ἴσῳ γὰρ τρόπῳ προσκεκόμικεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπέρ τε μικρῶν καὶ μεγάλων, λαοῦ τε καὶ ἱερέων ὁ Ἐμμανουήλ. Ἢ οὐκ ἀληθὲς ὅ φημι; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς γὰρ οὔ; {ΚΥΡ.} Βούλει δὴ οὖν ὥσπερ ἀνόπιν τὸν λόγον ἀνασειράζοντες, πρὸς τὰ ἐπὶ τῇ σκηνῇ διηγήματα μετατρεπώμεθα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Συμπεπερασμένων τοιγαροῦν τῶν ἔργων ἁπάντων, καὶ ἐν τόπῳ τῷ ἑκάστῳ πρεπωδεστάτῳ τῶν ἱερῶν σκευῶν εὖ μάλα συντεθειμένων, ἁγιάζεσθαι δεῖν αὐτά τε καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν διετύπου Θεὸς, οὕτω λέγων τῷ θεσπεσίῳ Μωσῇ· «Καὶ λήψῃ τὸ ἔλαιον τοῦ χρίσματος, καὶ χρίσεις τὴν σκηνὴν, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ἁγιάσεις αὐτὴν, καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτῆς, καὶ ἔσται ἅγια. Καὶ χρίσεις τὸ θυσιαστήριον τῶν καρπωμάτων, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ σκεύη, καὶ ἁγιάσεις τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καὶ ἔσται τὸ θυσιαστήριον Ἅγιον ἁγίων.» Ἐλαίῳ δὴ οὖν τῷ ἁγίῳ καταχριουμένην ὁρᾷς τήν τε κιβωτὸν, καὶ μέντοι τὴν τράπεζαν, καὶ τὴν λυχνίαν ἐπ' αὐτῇ, καὶ τὸ χρυσοῦν ἔτι θυμιατήριον· καί τοι γὰρ πάντων μακρὸς ἡμῖν διεσάφησεν ἤδη λόγος ἀνατυπούμενον τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Σύνες δὴ οὖν ἄρα τὸ διὰ φωνῆς τοῦ Δαβὶδ, ὡς πρὸς αὐτὸν ὑμνούμενον· «Ἠγάπησας δικαιοσύνην, καὶ ἐμίσησας ἀδικίαν. Διὰ τοῦτο ἔχρισέ σε Θεὸς, ὁ Θεός σου, ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους σου.» Γράφει δὲ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος, «ὅ τε γὰρ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι, ἐξ ἑνὸς πάντες.» Ἰστέον δὲ, ὅτι κατὰ τὸν ἀμωμήτως ἔχοντα λόγον, αὐτὸς ὑπάρχων ὁ
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing: poured out by the base of the altar of burnt offerings] in the first tent (πρώτη σκηνή); and the blood [is] into a type of the soul/life (ψυχή). Emmanuel has laid down (τίθημι) the soul not only for the Church from the nations (ἔθνη), but also for those in law, that is, Israel; for we have been ransomed (ἐκλυτρόω) by the blood of Christ all together (συλλήβδην), Greeks and Jews, and Paul will witness saying: 'Or is God of Jews only? not also of nations? yes, of nations too, since God is one, who will justify (δικαιόω) circumcision from faith and uncircumcision through faith'. The entrails (ἐντόσθια) of the calf being removed (ὑφαιρέω) and carried up (ἀναφέρω) to the altar, outside the camp (παρεμβολή) the remaining body is burned (καταπίμπρημι). For he is the holy victim (θῦμα), fragrant in virtues (ἀρεταί), of which the entrails would be types, and the virtues are as it were hidden (κρύπτω) in us and lying within into the mind (νοῦς); he also is the one suffering outside the gate (πύλη), and by the death of his own flesh cleansing (ἐκκαθαίρω) the defiled: 'For ashes (σποδός) of a heifer (δάμαλις) sprinkling the defiled (κοινόω) sanctify toward the purity of the flesh'. So Emmanuel, being one and the same, is fragrant in the holy tents, I mean the Churches; and he suffered outside the gate, where also we must go out bearing his reproach (ὀνειδισμός), the divine (θεσπέσιος) Paul said. The calf is brought also for the ignorances (ἀγνοήματα) of the people, equally and without variation (ἀπαραλλάκτως); and the rationale (λόγος) of the sacrifice was the same in all. For in equal manner Emmanuel has offered (προσκομίζω) himself for small and great, people and priests. Or is what I say not true? PALL. How not? CYR. Do you wish, as it were reining back (ἀνασειράζω) the account backwards (ἀνόπιν), we turn to the narratives (διηγήματα) about the tent? PALL. Very much. CYR. All the works being finished, and the holy vessels (σκεύη) well arranged each in the most fitting place, God prescribed (διατυπόω) that they and the tent must be sanctified, saying to divine Moses: 'And you will take the oil of anointing (χρίσμα), and anoint the tent and all things in it, and sanctify it and all its vessels, and they will be holy. And you will anoint the altar of burnt offerings and all vessels in it, and sanctify the altar, and the altar will be Holy of holies'. You see the ark anointed with holy oil, and the table (τράπεζα), and the lampstand (λυχνία) at it, and the golden censer (θυμιατήριον); and indeed a long account has made clear to us Emmanuel being figured (ἀνατυπόω) in all. PALL. True. CYR. Understand then the thing hymned (ὑμνέω) through the voice of David as to him: 'You loved righteousness and hated injustice (ἀδικία); therefore God, your God, anointed you with oil of gladness (ἀγαλλίασις) beyond your partners (μέτοχοι)'. pass_b_english: Cyril: …in the outer tent. The blood stands as a type of life (Leviticus 17:11), and Emmanuel has laid down his life (John 10:15) not only for the Church from the Gentiles but also for those under the law, that is, for Israel. For all of us together, Greeks and Jews alike, have been redeemed by the blood of Christ, and Paul will bear witness, saying: ‘Or is God the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also, since God is one, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith’ (Romans 3:29–30). When the inner parts of the calf have been taken out and carried up to the altar (Leviticus 4:8–10), the rest of the body is burned outside the camp (Leviticus 4:11–12). For he himself is the holy sacrifice, fragrant with virtues, of which the inner parts would be types, since the virtues are hidden, as it were, within us and lie deep within the mind. He is also the one who suffers outside the gate (Hebrews 13:12), and by the death of his own flesh cleanses those who were defiled. For ‘the ashes of a heifer, sprinkled on those who are defiled,’ it says, ‘sanctify for the purification of the flesh’ (Hebrews 9:13). So Emmanuel, being one and the same, gives off his fragrance in the holy tents, I mean the churches, and he also suffered outside the gate; and there, as the inspired Paul said, we too must go out, bearing his reproach (Hebrews 13:13). A calf is also brought for the sins of ignorance of the people (Leviticus 4:13–14), in the same way and without any difference, and the meaning of the sacrifice was the same in every case. For Emmanuel offered himself in the same way for small and great, for people and priests alike. Or is what I say not true?
Palladius: How could it not be?
Cyril: Shall we, then, rein the discussion back, as it were, and turn again to the accounts of the tent?

Cyril: When all the work had been completed, and each of the holy vessels had been carefully set in the place most fitting for it, God laid down that they and the tent must be sanctified, saying to the inspired Moses: ‘And you shall take the oil of anointing, and anoint the tent and everything in it, and you shall sanctify it and all its vessels, and they shall be holy. And you shall anoint the altar of burnt offerings and all its vessels, and you shall sanctify the altar, and the altar shall be holy of holies’ (Exodus 40:9–10). So you see the ark anointed with the holy oil, and the table too, and the lampstand beside it, and the golden altar of incense as well; and indeed our long discussion has already made clear that in all of them Emmanuel is portrayed.

Cyril: Consider, then, what is sung by the voice of David as addressed to him: ‘You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions’ (Psalm 45:7). anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-phrase: ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ completes 'the altar of burnt offerings' from section 20. 'The first tent' (Hebrews 9:2, 6 language) is rendered 'the outer tent' for clarity. ψυχή is rendered 'life' twice ('a type of the life', 'laid down his life') to keep Cyril's link between the blood and Christ's self-giving; Leviticus 17:11 (ἡ ψυχὴ πάσης σαρκὸς αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐστιν) is cited as the evident basis for 'blood = soul/life'. 'Laid down his life' cited to John 10:15 (τὴν ψυχήν μου τίθημι). 'Redeemed by the blood of Christ' may echo 1 Peter 1:18-19 or Ephesians 1:7; left uncited as general. Hebrews is quoted as Paul's, as Cyril regards it. ἐντόσθια = the inner parts (fat, kidneys, liver lobe of Leviticus 4:8-10). Hebrews 13:13 is paraphrased without 'to him' (πρὸς αὐτόν), as Cyril has it. Exodus 40:9-10: verse numbers agree in LXX and English. ἅγιον ἁγίων is kept as 'holy of holies' (not 'most holy') because section 22 builds on the phrase, calling the law 'holy of holies' and Christ 'the Holy of Holies'. Psalm 45:7 = LXX Psalm 44:8 (LXX numbering converted). ἀδικία rendered 'lawlessness' following the usual English of this verse; literally 'injustice/wrongdoing'. The section ends mid-sentence ('αὐτὸς ὑπάρχων ὁ | τοῖς ἄλλοις ...'), continued in section 22.

changes: Joined the μέν/δέ pair: 'a type of life, and Emmanuel has laid down his life' (perfect τέθεικε)
Removed added 'gathered' (τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησίας = 'the Church from the Gentiles', as in section 22)
'lie inward in the mind' -> 'lie deep within the mind'
Hebrews 9:13 'purity' -> 'purification of the flesh' (smoother English, same sense)
Psalm 45:7: ἀδικίαν rendered 'wickedness' (Cyril reads ἀδικίαν, not LXX ἀνομίαν; 'lawlessness' matched the wrong word); 'as though to him' -> 'as addressed to him'
'on a reckoning that admits no fault' -> 'by reasoning free from all fault'

Citations checked: Lev 17:11 (basis of blood = life), John 10:15, Rom 3:29-30, Lev 4:8-10, 4:11-12, 4:13-14, Heb 13:12, 9:13, 13:13, Exod 40:9-10 (same in LXX and English), Ps 45:7 = LXX 44:8, Heb 2:11: correct
